newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police arrest 15 for Corsican violence.
newsitem.headline: French police arrest 15 for Corsican violence.

text.p: Fifteen people have been arrested in connection with two bomb attacks by Corsican separatists in the southern French city of Aix-en-Provence last year, police said on Wednesday.
The arrests took place on Tuesday and Wednesday in Corsica and in the mainland Mediterranean port of Marseille, which has a large Corsican population.
The attacks in Aix, against the local law courts and a post office, in September and November respectively, caused no casualties but there was widespread damage.
Corsican separatists, who carried out several hundred bomb attacks on the Mediterranean island last year, generally scrupulously avoid casualties by detonating their explosive devices late at night.
No other details were immediately available about the arrests. The outlawed Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC) Historic Wing last year claimed responsibility for the Aix attacks.

The same group exploded 76 small devices in Corsica on Sunday in a show of strength which followed a police crackdown against them in the past weeks. Three of its main political leaders are in detention.

No one was injured in Sunday's coordinated pre-dawn blitz of tiny blasts. Damage was mostly limited to smashed windows or damaged doorways at post offices, tax offices and other symbols of French state authority in towns and villages.
